# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can feel the button’s raised label: “PUSH TO DEFUSE.” I cannot detect any wire properties or other tactile markings. The manual reader should determine whether that instruction is safe and tell me which operation, if any, to perform. I have no useful visual fact to encode for Deaf yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I can feel the button's raised label: PUSH TO DEFUSE. I cannot detect any wire properties or other tactile markings. Please consult the manual and tell me whether to push it or cut a wire.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visual bomb state: display reads 0. Indicator light is yellow. There is a large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires are 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green.

I now know the visible state through Deaf: display 0, yellow indicator, and wires 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. I still do not know the manual’s rule, so I must not touch the bomb. I will relay the full state to Mute and ask for the required safe operation.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 0, yellow indicator, and wires: 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. What does the manual require?")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's new visual message was: first ?, the I-love-you hand sign; second ?, the two-finger V sign. The bomb remains display 0, yellow light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires red-blue-green.

Mute’s gestures appear to be 🤟 and ✌, but no meaning has been established for them. I cannot see gestures, so I cannot safely infer an operation from them. I will ask Mute to have Deaf verbally describe the manual’s actual instruction or its meaning.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot see your gestures, and their meanings are not established. Please communicate the manual's instruction to Deaf in a way Deaf can describe verbally to me next turn.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No bomb change. Mute again signaled ? then ?, in that order. Meaning is not established.

The repeated 🤟 then ✌ has not conveyed an established instruction, so acting would be unsafe. I will establish a one-gesture code that Mute can use to transmit the manual’s required operation through Deaf: thumbs-up means push, index-up means cut wire 1, V means cut wire 2, and I-love-you means cut wire 3. Mute should choose exactly one based on the manual and send only that gesture.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use exactly one gesture to report the manual's required action: thumbs-up means PUSH; index-up means CUT wire 1; V means CUT wire 2; I-love-you means CUT wire 3. Choose the one required for display 0, yellow light, and wires red-blue-green. Do not send two gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No bomb change. Mute signaled ? then ?: thumbs-down, then V sign. Under my tentative code this could mean light, wire 2, but that code is unconfirmed; do not act on it yet.

The reported pair is specifically 👎 followed by ✌. It is still unsafe to treat an ad hoc interpretation as authorization, especially because Mute has not followed the one-gesture convention. I will establish an unambiguous two-part code: first gesture identifies whether to push or cut, and the second identifies the wire. Mute should repeat the pair only if the manual requires cutting wire 2; otherwise use the specified alternative.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Do not use an unrequested code. Use exactly this confirmed format: for PUSH, signal 👍 alone; for CUT, signal 👎 followed by the wire number gesture: ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3. Your reported 👎 then ✌ would mean CUT wire 2. Repeat 👎 then ✌ only if the manual explicitly requires cutting wire 2; otherwise signal the correct format.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest signal is ? (the V/two-finger sign). The sequence received so far is ? ?, then ? ?, then ?. No bomb state has changed.

The latest V gesture alone is not sufficient: under the agreed code, a cut requires both the cut marker and a wire marker. No action has been authorized, and the bomb is unchanged. I will require Mute to send exactly one complete code, with no extra gestures.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="No action yet. Send exactly one complete code and nothing else: 👍 means PUSH; 👎 then ☝ means CUT wire 1; 👎 then ✌ means CUT wire 2; 👎 then 🤟 means CUT wire 3. Do not send a wire gesture by itself.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current signal from Mute: ? then ? (thumbs-down, then V/two-finger sign). Complete received sequence by round: ? ?; ? ?; ? ?; ?; ? ?. Bomb still shows display 0, yellow light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, and wires red, blue, green.

Mute has now sent the exact agreed code 👎 then ✌, which means cut wire 2. The bomb state remains display 0 with yellow light and wires red-blue-green; I will perform that authorized operation.

```text
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
